feature: Measurements wear the same chip styles, colour and marker as an arrow label
summary: A size, gap, distance or alignment readout can now wear any of the ten chip styles, one Color for caliper and chip, and a marker, picked the same way as on an arrow's label: on the picked measurement, in the Measure tool's settings for the next one, or from its right-click menu.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/measure-chip-styles-walk.json.

try.do: Open a screenshot, press I, set Mode to Gap and click between two lines of text.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick the Gap in the Measurements list and look at Appearance: Chip, Color and Marker rows, Today lit.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the Paper tile, then the warning triangle in the Marker row (or right-click the measurement: Chip Style > Paper, Chip Marker > Warning).
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Zoom in on the readout: the caliper stops on the card's edge.
Click a swatch in the Color row: caliper and chip change together.
Press Command-Z once: only the last change goes back.
Click empty canvas and measure another gap: it comes out on Paper with the warning.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Does a measurement on Paper or Spec badge read as part of the same redline as an arrow label on the same style?
Should a new measurement keep its old navy pill until you pick a style, or start on Solid like a new arrow does?
Is the warning icon at the readout's front useful on a measurement, or only on arrows?
Do Chip Style and Chip Marker belong on the measurement's right-click menu?
rough: Measured contrast, read off the rendered pixels: every style in five colours (the measurement blue, red, yellow, near-black and a custom light green) over white, black and a busy photo, 150 readings, lowest 4.58:1 (Hairline in yellow over black). All lines: 2026-11-01-measure-chip-styles-contrast.tsv.

Under a walk, a press on the Chip tiles, Marker buttons and Color swatches does nothing, the same dead press the arrow's rows have had since 2026-10-26 (walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-26). So the walk picks Paper and Warning from the right-click menu, and the Color row and the Reset Colors warning are proven by tests, not yet by a walk's click.

A new measurement keeps the pill it always had, which the Chip row calls Today, until a style is picked; a new arrow starts on Solid. I chose this because the measurement look was sampled from your own screenshot on 2026-10-13.
No Size (S, M, L) row and no Advanced fold yet: the chip's Fill, Edge and Text rows still sit open below Marker, as they do on an arrow (arrow-and-measurement-appearance-shows-only-styl).

With the Measure tool in hand and a measurement picked, the Measure Tool section stays open above Appearance, so Appearance gets less of the dock and its Color swatches, Marker row and part rows start below its fold; scroll the section to reach them.
Every picture is the window behind another app, so picked tiles show their background look; the canvas is what was drawn.
